modeReason: Three stories clear the relevance threshold of 8: the school-AI-claims-vs-data gap and the political-bias study each score 3×2×2=12, and the platform's AI-and-human threat-monitoring story scores 2×2×3=12, so today stands on its own rather than continuing yesterday's thread.
phrase: A school network claims AI teaches kids twice as fast. Half its K-8 students missed that goal in math — the same week economists found no AI payoff outside tech.
phraseAlternatives: One school network says its AI helps kids learn twice as fast. New data show half its K-8 students fell short in math — and so has the wider economy.
A school claims AI makes learning twice as fast. Half its K-8 students missed the mark in math, just as economists found AI still is not paying off outside tech.
Outside the classroom and outside the tech industry, AI's biggest promises are not yet adding up, according to this week's data and economics.

brief.concept: A school's AI tutor promises to double how fast children learn, but only half the class reaches the goal line, while in a parallel scene a company keeps feeding coins into a glowing AI box without its profit arrow ever rising.
brief.metaphor: A classroom goal line that half the students don't reach stands in for every AI promise that outruns its results.
